question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scari" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Scary", meaning frightening or causing fear. (डरावना)

◦ Correct: The dark, empty house looked very scary.

• Spelling key: SCA + RY (the "-y" ending, not "-i").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "Reflect" (to throw back light/an image; to think deeply), "Music" (vocal or instrumental sounds) and "Shadow" (a dark shape produced by a body blocking light).

NOTE

• Adjectives formed from nouns often end in "-y": scare → scary, fear → (no), rain → rainy, cloud → cloudy. Do not end them with "-i".

question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rohit Sharma is better than more other batsman in the world.
option_4: as good as the most other batsmen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. better than most other batsmen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative structure "better than most other + plural noun" is the correct way to compare one member with the rest of a group. So "better than most other batsmen" is right; "more other batsman" is wrong (wrong word "more" and singular "batsman").

◦ Correct: Rohit Sharma is better than most other batsmen in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the best batsmen" changes the degree to superlative and drops "than".

• Option 2 "better batsmen" is incomplete (no "than most other").

• Option 4 "as good as the most other batsmen" mixes positive degree with a wrong superlative and is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Comparative pattern for one vs. the rest: "X is + comparative + than + most/any other + plural noun" (e.g., "faster than most other runners").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The analysis of a person's handwriting to determine his/her personality
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Graphology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Graphology" is the study/analysis of handwriting, especially as used to assess a person's character or personality. (लिखावट का अध्ययन)

◦ Example: A graphologist studied the note to describe the writer's temperament.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Numismatics" — the study of coins and currency.

• Option 3 "Philology" — the study of the history and structure of languages.

• Option 4 "Calligraphy" — the art of beautiful/decorative handwriting.

NOTE

• Related "-logy/-graphy" terms: Cartography (map-making), Orography (mountains), Etymology (origin of words), Genealogy (family lineage).

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: Rukmini put a book on an table and sat down.
option_2: Rukmini put an book on the table and sat down.
option_3: Rukmini put the book on an table and sat down.
option_4: Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "an" is used only before a vowel sound; "table" begins with a consonant sound, so "an table" is wrong. The specific, known objects here take the definite article "the": the book, the table.

◦ Correct: Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a book on an table" and Option 3 "on an table" wrongly use "an" before a consonant sound.

• Option 2 "an book" is wrong for the same reason (book starts with a consonant sound).

NOTE

• Use "a" before a consonant sound (a book, a table), "an" before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour), and "the" for specific/already-known nouns.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Anupama was a very industrious child and submitted all her assignments on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. lazy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Industrious" means hard-working and diligent. Its antonym is "lazy" (unwilling to work or make effort). (परिश्रमी का विलोम — आलसी)

◦ Example: An industrious student works hard, while a lazy one avoids effort.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laborious" (requiring much effort) is closer to a synonym.

• Option 3 "industrial" (relating to industry) is a distractor that looks similar but is unrelated.

• Option 4 "intense" (very strong/extreme) does not fit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of industrious: diligent, hard-working, assiduous, sedulous. Antonyms: lazy, idle, indolent, slothful.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

I bought a _____ but it is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. chip; cheap.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs a noun for the first blank (the thing bought) and an adjective for the second. "chip" (a small object/snack/microchip) is the noun and "cheap" (low in price) is the adjective. (मैंने एक चिप खरीदी पर वह सस्ती है)

◦ Correct: I bought a chip but it is cheap.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "cain" is not a standard English word; "cane" means a walking stick or a stem (bamboo/sugar cane) — a noun, so it cannot fill the adjective blank correctly.

• Options 1 and 4 use "cain", which is not a valid word here; Option 3 reverses the order (cheap; chip), giving "I bought a cheap but it is chip" which is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Watch for homophone/near-homophone pairs (chip/cheap, cane/cain): pick the one that fits the required part of speech and meaning.

question:
Identify the error in the given sentence.

Ajit got to work earliest than everyone else today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. earliest than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree, but "earliest" is the superlative. The comparative of "early" is "earlier". So it should be "earlier than".

◦ Correct: Ajit got to work earlier than everyone else today.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "today", "everyone else" and "Ajit got to work" are all correct.

• Superlatives ("earliest") take "the" and are used to compare three or more, not with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of "early": early – earlier (with "than") – earliest (with "the"). Never use a superlative with "than".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The happy and cheerful girls / is always running towards / the ice cream cart in / front of the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is always running towards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "girls" is plural, so it needs the plural verb "are", not the singular "is". So it should be "are always running towards".

◦ Correct: The happy and cheerful girls are always running towards the ice cream cart in front of the garden.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "the happy and cheerful girls", "the ice cream cart in" and "front of the garden" are all correct.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a plural subject (girls, boys, they) takes are/were/have; a singular subject (girl, he) takes is/was/has.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Are you sure that you can't even write a single sentnce properly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sentnce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "sentnce" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "sentence" (a set of words that is complete in itself, expressing a statement, question, etc.). (वाक्य)

◦ Correct: Are you sure that you can't even write a single sentence properly?

• Spelling key: SEN + TENCE (an "e" between the "t" and "n" — "sen-TEN-ce").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "single" (one only), "write" (to form letters/words) and "properly" (correctly) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words: sentence, definitely, separate, necessary, occurrence. Break long words into syllables to spell them correctly.

question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Maheshwari is three years junior than me.
option_3: junior than any other to me
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. junior to me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Latin-origin comparatives such as "junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior, posterior" are followed by "to", never "than". So it must be "junior to me".

◦ Correct: Maheshwari is three years junior to me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "junior than that of me" and Option 3 "junior than any other to me" wrongly use "than" and are clumsy.

• Option 2 "more junior than me" is wrong because "junior" already carries a comparative sense and takes "to", not "more ... than".

NOTE

• Remember the "-ior + to" rule: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, prior to, prefer (X) to (Y).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Beginer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beginer" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Beginner" (a person who is just starting to learn something). (नौसिखिया / शुरुआती)

◦ Correct: As a beginner, she practised for an hour daily.

• Spelling key: the final consonant "n" is doubled before "-er": begin → beginner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Prescription" (a doctor's written instruction), "Ceremony" (a formal event) and "Disappointment" (sadness from unmet hopes) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Doubling rule: in a stressed final syllable ending in a single vowel + single consonant, double the consonant before "-er/-ing/-ed": begin → beginner, refer → referred, prefer → preferred.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The branch of geography that studies mountains and their formation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Orography.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Orography" is the branch of geography (physical geography) that studies mountains, hills and their formation. (पर्वतों का अध्ययन)

◦ Example: Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to rise over mountains.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Palaeography" — the study of ancient writing/scripts.

• Option 2 "Orthography" — the study of correct spelling.

• Option 4 "Mythography" — the collection/study of myths.

NOTE

• The root "oro-" means mountain (e.g., orogeny = mountain-building, orographic rainfall = rain caused by mountains).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The students were __________ for their hard work with certificates and praise.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rewarded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rewarded" means given something in recognition of good work/effort. Since the students received "certificates and praise" for their "hard work", they were rewarded. (पुरस्कृत किया गया)

◦ Correct: The students were rewarded for their hard work with certificates and praise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "reprimanded" (scolded formally), 2 "penalised" (punished/fined) and 4 "punished" all carry a negative sense and contradict "certificates and praise".

NOTE

• "Reward" collocates with positive effort (rewarded for hard work); "punish/penalise/reprimand" collocate with wrongdoing.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: Rahul is very naughty as he is the most young sibling between Rama's three brothers.
option_2: Rahul is very naughty as he is the youngest sibling among Rama's three brothers.
option_3: Rahul is very naughty as he is the youngest sibling between Rama's three brothers.
option_4: Rahul is very naughty as he is the most young sibling among Rama's three brothers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rahul is very naughty as he is the youngest sibling among Rama's three brothers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two rules apply: (i) the superlative of "young" is "youngest", not "most young"; (ii) "among" is used for more than two (three brothers), while "between" is used for two.

◦ Correct: ... he is the youngest sibling among Rama's three brothers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 wrongly use "most young" instead of "youngest".

• Options 1 and 3 wrongly use "between" for three brothers.

NOTE

• Short adjectives form the superlative with "-est" (young → youngest), not "most". Use "between" for two and "among" for three or more.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The concert was __________ due to the bad weather.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cancelled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cancelled" means called off / not held. Because of "bad weather", the concert was most logically cancelled. (रद्द किया गया)

◦ Correct: The concert was cancelled due to the bad weather.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "celebrated", Option 2 "continued" and Option 4 "commenced" (began) all suggest the event went ahead, which contradicts "bad weather".

NOTE

• Note the double "l" (British): cancelled / cancelling, but the noun is cancellation. American spelling: canceled.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He was very inquisitive and wanted to know each and every detail.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Indifferent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inquisitive" means curious and eager to know. Its antonym is "indifferent" (having no interest or concern). (जिज्ञासु का विलोम — उदासीन)

◦ Example: An inquisitive child asks many questions; an indifferent one shows no interest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Uncanny" (strange/mysterious), Option 3 "Indeterminate" (not fixed/vague) and Option 4 "Intelligent" (clever) are not antonyms of inquisitive.

NOTE

• Synonyms of inquisitive: curious, prying, questioning. Antonyms: indifferent, uninterested, apathetic, incurious.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment.

He thinks his new plan will undoubtedly produce the desired result.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bear fruit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bear fruit" means to produce good/successful results. It fits "produce the desired result". (सफल होना / फल देना)

◦ Correct: He thinks his new plan will undoubtedly bear fruit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "go suck a lemon" (a rude way of dismissing someone), Option 3 "sour grapes" (pretending to dislike what one cannot have) and Option 4 "go pear-shaped" (to go wrong / fail) do not mean "succeed".

NOTE

• Idioms of success: "bear fruit", "pay off", "come to fruition". Idioms of failure: "go pear-shaped", "fall through", "come to nothing".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Antique
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ancient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Antique" means belonging to ancient/earlier times; very old and often valuable. Its closest synonym is "ancient". (प्राचीन)

◦ Example: The museum displayed antique/ancient coins and pottery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Novel" (new/original), Option 2 "Young" and Option 4 "Modern" are all antonyms of antique.

NOTE

• Synonyms of antique: ancient, old, vintage, archaic. Antonyms: modern, new, contemporary, novel.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Many orthodox people have a ____(hostile) attitude towards the idea of women getting educated and employed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. belligerent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hostile" means unfriendly, aggressive or opposed. Its closest synonym is "belligerent" (aggressive, ready to fight/oppose). (शत्रुतापूर्ण / आक्रामक)

◦ Correct: Many orthodox people have a belligerent attitude towards the idea of women getting educated and employed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "friendly" is an antonym.

• Option 3 "meticulous" (very careful about detail) and Option 4 "elaborate" (detailed/complicated) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hostile: belligerent, antagonistic, aggressive, unfriendly. Antonyms: friendly, cordial, amicable.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Losing my job turned out to be an unexpected benefit because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a blessing in disguise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a blessing in disguise" means something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good. Losing the job (bad) led to a successful business (good) — an "unexpected benefit". (छिपा हुआ वरदान)

◦ Correct: Losing my job turned out to be a blessing in disguise because it pushed me to start my own business ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a golden opportunity" (an excellent chance) misses the "seemed bad first" element.

• Option 2 "a diamond in the rough" (someone/thing with hidden good qualities) does not fit.

• Option 4 "a mixed blessing" (having both good and bad sides) is not the same as a purely positive outcome.

NOTE

• "A blessing in disguise" always implies an initially negative event with an ultimately positive result.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer-controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. endanger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says the computer "can become a threat to man", so it must harm/put at risk his survival and privacy. "Endanger" means to put in danger/at risk. (ख़तरे में डालना)

◦ Correct: It can endanger his survival and privacy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tranformative" is a misspelling and is an adjective, not a verb; it does not fit.

• Option 2 "protect" and Option 4 "encourage" are positive and contradict "threat".

NOTE

• Watch the tone of the passage: negative context ("threat") demands a negative verb ("endanger"), not a positive one.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer-controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. worsen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Because employers "prefer the computer and 'computer-controlled robots' to humans", jobs are lost, so the computer makes the unemployment problem worse. "Worsen" means to make worse. (बदतर बनाना)

◦ Correct: It can worsen the unemployment problem ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "control" and 2 "improve" wrongly suggest a positive effect on unemployment.

• Option 4 "beat" does not collocate meaningfully with "the unemployment problem" here.

NOTE

• The clause "as employers prefer the computer ... to humans" signals a negative consequence, so "worsen" fits the cause–effect logic.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer-controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. led.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "lead to" means to result in / cause. The storage facility "has led to collection ... and storage of information in data banks". The following word "to" confirms this collocation. (के कारण होना)

◦ Correct: The information storage facility ... has led to collection of personal information ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "involved", 2 "stored" and 4 "experienced" do not fit the fixed structure "has ___ to".

NOTE

• "Lead – led – led" (to cause a result): "Hard work led to success." Do not confuse with the metal "lead".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer-controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. during.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "During" is a preposition meaning throughout the course of / in the process of. "If care is not exercised during data gathering" correctly means "while the data is being gathered". (के दौरान)

◦ Correct: If care is not exercised during data gathering, data integrity may suffer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "when" and Option 4 "unless" are conjunctions and would need a clause (subject + verb), not the noun phrase "data gathering".

• Option 3 "by" changes the meaning (agency/means), which does not fit "care is not exercised ___ data gathering".

NOTE

• "During + noun/noun phrase" (during the meeting, during data gathering); "while + clause" (while data is being gathered).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer-controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. may.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage speaks of a possibility ("incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this ... become a permanent source"). The modal "may" expresses possibility and keeps the tone tentative, matching the earlier "may suffer" and "may be stored". (सकता है — संभावना)

◦ Correct: ... and this may become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "must" and 4 "have to" express strong obligation/certainty, which is too strong here.

• Option 3 "should" expresses advice/expectation, which does not fit the sense of possibility.

NOTE

• Modals of possibility: may, might, could. Modals of obligation/certainty: must, have to, need to. The passage's cautious tone needs "may".
